steps.title: Performance Enhancing Drugs (PEDs)
steps.body: Substances used to improve sporting performance that are banned by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA). Taking PEDs is considered cheating because it gives an unfair advantage over clean competitors.

steps.title: Stimulants
steps.body: Drugs that increase alertness, reduce fatigue and increase aggression and competitiveness. They speed up the activity of the central nervous system.

steps.title: Narcotic Analgesics
steps.body: Painkilling drugs that mask the sensation of pain, allowing performers to continue training or competing despite injury. They work by blocking pain signals to the brain.

steps.title: Anabolic Agents
steps.body: Drugs that mimic the effects of the male hormone testosterone, promoting muscle growth (hypertrophy) and increasing strength. They also speed up recovery from intense training.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know all six drug types PLUS blood doping - their effects, advantages AND side effects Match each PED to an appropriate sport - EPO = cycling, beta blockers = archery, anabolic steroids = weightlifting Explain HOW each drug works, not just what it does Diuretics have two uses: weight loss AND masking other drugs - know both Blood doping and EPO have similar results but different methods - distinguish them Always discuss both advantages and disadvantages when evaluating PEDs
